**[p-300]** **Surah al-Kafirun**

It is also called al-Ikhlas (Sincerity) and al-Muqashqisha (The Cleanser).

Its purpose is to establish the purpose of al-Kawthar, through the evidence of witnessing, on the One who possesses complete knowledge and comprehensive power, because He alone is singular in unity (tawhid, the oneness of God). Therefore, whoever is with Him cannot oppose Him. For this reason, when it was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it [to them -] in the mosque, all of them being present. This is the meaning of each of its names. As for "al-Kafirun" (The Disbelievers), it has two aspects: one looking to affirmation and one looking to negation. The affirmative aspect is that it points to contemplating the whole surah, by applying the part to the whole. The negative aspect is that they disbelieved only by denying what is its purpose, either explicitly, such as the unity of God and the completeness of His power, or by necessary implication, which is the "amm" (the general sense of the matter), since whoever diminishes His power necessarily diminishes Him. As for "al-Ikhlas" (Sincerity), it is because whoever believes this is [a believer -] sincere, free from every association (shirk) and every disbelief (kufr). As for "al-Muqashqisha" (The Cleanser), it is because it cleansed one of every hypocrisy and disbelief, from the saying of them: "his sores were scabbed (tadaqshaqat) when they peeled off for healing." In my view it is also from gathering, taking from the "qash" (straw), which is seeking food from here and there, because it gathered **[p-301]** all the foundations of the religion and affirmed them in the most complete manner. It follows from this that it gathered all types of disbelief, and so it removed them and negated them. The full explanation of this has already been mentioned in Surah Bara'a (al-Tawbah). The matter of both surahs revolves around sincerity. It is known that whoever is sincere to God is truly among the people of His guardianship (wilayah), so he has the right to be treated as a friend treats his friend. For this reason, God knows best, it was prescribed to recite it together with ﴿Say: He is God, One﴾ [al-Ikhlas: 1] in the two rak'ahs of the dawn prayer, so that whoever does this may begin the day with freedom from shirk and with the attribute of tawhid, as the fruit of what has been reported: whoever prays the dawn prayer is under the protection of God. Whoever is like this is worthy of attaining what the two surahs between the two surahs of Ikhlas point to: victory and support for him, defeat for his enemy, and loss and regret for him. [They are]: "In the name of God" (Bismillah), who encompasses all in knowledge and power; He is the One whom no one can estimate according to His true measure. "The Most Gracious" (al-Rahman), who by the mercy of exposition has embraced those upon whom He made obligatory their gratitude to Him. "The Most Merciful" (al-Rahim), who has singled out the people of His love, so they adhered to His prohibitions and His commands.

* *

Because He informed him in al-Kawthar that the one who hates him is cut off (ʿadam), it became necessary that he turn away from him and turn wholly toward the One who bestowed this blessing upon him. So He said, informing him of what he should say and do: ﴿Say﴾. And since his enemy's condition was the most deeply rooted of creation in misguidance and distance from good, He addressed him with the particle of distance, although he was present, and expressed it by the descriptive term that indicates firm establishment: ﴿O you disbelievers﴾, that is, those whose disbelief has been decreed as firmly fixed, so there is no release for them from it. Thus they concealed what their intellects indicate of the true belief, if they stripped them of the impurities of their fortune. They are specific disbelievers, those whose death upon disbelief has been decreed, in accordance with what corresponds to reality and with what the expression by a descriptive term rather than a verb indicates. The definite article (al-) encompasses everyone who is of this description, in every place and every time. He expressed it with the plural, which is originally used for few, though it may be borrowed for many, as an indication of the good news of the small number among the Arabs addressed by this in his lifetime (ﷺ) whose hearts were sealed, and as an indication of the lowliness and humiliation of the disbeliever, even if they are many. This is as indicated by making each word of it correspond to a letter of al-Kawthar, as will come. In addressing them with this descriptive term, which they despise, in their own town and place of their honour and zeal, there is an announcement that he is protected from them, as one of the signs of prophethood.

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When the mention of the two groups, whose mention recurs in the Noble Book from its beginning to its end, had been completed, with the differences of each group's conditions and their various ranks, and by "the two groups" I mean those referred to in His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾ [al-Fatihah: 6] ﴿the path of those upon whom You have bestowed favour﴾ [al-Fatihah: 7]. This is the path of one of the two groups. And in His saying: ﴿not of those who have earned anger, nor of those who are astray﴾ [al-Fatihah: 7], **[p-303]** there is an indication of the path of those at the other extreme from the condition of those people, since there is only the path of safety or the path of destruction: ﴿a group in the Garden and a group in the Blaze﴾ [al-Shura: 7], ﴿Among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer﴾ [al-Taghabun: 2]. Those who travel the path of safety, the highest of their ranks are the stations of the messengers and prophets, peace and blessings be upon them. Then come their followers from the righteous servants and their scholars who act, their worshippers, the people of special closeness, and those close to the states of those who are ascetic among them. Their ranks vary, even though one comprehensive term gathers them, which is His saying: ﴿a group in the Garden﴾ [al-Shura: 7]. As for those who deviate from this path, who are the ruined, they too are in levels, yet one path gathers all of them. Thus, however the ways branch out, they return to the two paths mentioned. By the differing ways of all, you come to know which Book has been distinguished and detailed. It is all a mention in complete detail, leaving no doubt for whoever is granted success. When all of that was completed along with what pertains to it, and the verses had gone through its explanation from His saying, after the Mother of the Qur'an, ﴿a guidance for the God-fearing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 2], up to His saying: ﴿Indeed, your enemy is the one cut off﴾ [al-Kawthar: 3], He followed this with the particulars and the recording, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾. Thus He, glorified is He, made clear that whoever has been decreed to disbelief and to dying upon it has no way out of that, and faith never comes from him.

﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered against them all things face to face, they would not have believed unless God willed﴾ [al-An'am: 111]. And even if they, after the punishment of the Hereafter, and after witnessing the punishment and the resurrection and the great terrors of those horrors, and asked to return to the world, saying: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out, and we will do righteous deeds other than what we used to do﴾ [Fatir: 37], then if they were answered in this and returned, they would revert to their former condition: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 28], confirming the word of God and affirming His previous decree: ﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has been fulfilled, can you save whoever is in the Fire?﴾ [al-Zumar: 19]. So He said to them: ﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 2], ﴿nor are you worshippers of what I worship﴾ [al-Kafirun: 3], to the end of it. Thus the matter of the two groups became clear and the problem was resolved, and each continued on its own path. ﴿So let not your soul go to waste in regret over them﴾ [Fatir: 8], ﴿Your duty is only to deliver the message﴾ [al-Shura: 48]. So reflect on the position of this surah, and that it is the conclusion of what was intended in the Book; the wisdom of placing it last becomes apparent to you, God knows best. End.

When the aim was to inform them of his disassociation from them in every respect, and that he does not care for them in any way, because he is protected from them, He said, signifying the truth of His report, exalted is He, at the end of al-Kawthar, in that even with the certainty of standing apart from them, they are unable to inflict any effective harm upon him, beginning with disassociation from their side because it is the more important: ﴿I do not worship﴾, meaning now and not in the future, because "lā" is for the future and "mā" is for the present (al-ḥāl), so they said. The apparent sense of Sibawayh's expression, where he says "lan" is a negation of "sayafʿalu" and "lā" a negation of "yafʿalu", without specifying that it applies to the non-occurring imperfect whether it is at the closest point to the present or not, as I quoted him at the beginning of al-Baqarah at ﴿and you will never do it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 24], suggests the same. Moreover, our utterance of this statement hardly becomes realized until a time passes and it becomes future. Therefore he expressed it with "lā" rather than "mā", as good news that He, glory be to Him, will keep him upon the straight path and will not grant them victory over it, as one of the signs of prophethood.

Since among what they worshipped there were things that do not reason, and the intended aim was to belittle everything they worshipped besides God, He expressed it with "mā" and said: ﴿what you worship﴾, meaning now and in future time, apart from God, of the worshipped things, both apparent and hidden, in any of the forms of worship, in secret or openly, because it is not fit for worship in any way.

When he began with what is most deserving of priority, which is disavowal of polytheism and purification from the defamation of falsehood, since it is among the warding off of corruptions, he emphasized this with what is fitting for his own state (ﷺ). They were worshipping God Most High in the manner of associating partners, and worship accompanied by shirk is not counted as valid in any respect. So he negated their worship of Him in the nominal sentence (al-jumla al-ismiyya), which indicates permanence, rather than the verbal sentence (al-jumla al-fi'liyya), which indicates negation of every little and much, since [that] the verb is indefinite (nakira) in the context of negation. So he said: ﴿Nor are you worshippers﴾, meaning worship that is counted as valid, such that it would be fit to be a stable attribute.

(p-٣٠٦) When they had no dispute that their object of worship is knowing, and "ma" (what) is suitable to be applied to Him, glorified and exalted, he also expressed it with "ma" because that, although there is no harm in it, is closer to fairness, and so it is more conducive to avoiding dispute or disagreement. So he said: ﴿I do not worship﴾, meaning now and what follows, because my object of worship [and to Him belongs] complete knowledge and all-encompassing power, [has put you far from Him], so there is no hope of agreement between us.

Since what was negated of the Prophet ﷺ [does not include the past, and the absence of association in any form at any time is more indicative of innocence and more firmly establishes the continuance of contempt; and they used to consider his ﷺ silence concerning them -] before prophethood as worship, and they were not limited to worshipping their idols which they had taken; rather, when they went out of the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram) and alighted at a station, they looked for a stone for themselves to admire, so they would worship it. If they did not find a stone, they gathered some dirt, milked some milk over it, and worshipped it for as long as they remained at that station. This was among the most blameworthy things in respect of the lack of worthiness, and that they had no helpful deity (p-307) for them. He said, admonishing them concerning all of that: ﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾, meaning, one characterised by worship of ﴿what you have worshipped﴾, meaning in what has passed, the attribution to me of worshipping that has never been valid from the beginning of your time until this very hour of ours. So how do you expect that from me, when I have not done it, neither before prophethood, nor has it ever been my practice?

When he (ﷺ) was steadfast upon one God, whom none other was worshipped and to whom he never once turned, and when by these two past sentences at the beginning of the surah he had been cleared of worshipping their falsehood, whether presently or in the future, and of having been its servant before that, a speaker might have thought that the negation concerning them applied only to worshipping what they worship at present. So He negated it for the future as well, as one of the signs of prophethood, while reinforcing what the past sentence conveyed, following the methods of the Arabs in emphasis. This cuts off their hopes from him in the most complete and emphatic manner, since it is in a form they cannot achieve, because each sentence, with the emphasis, conveys a new and important benefit. So He said: ﴿And you will not be worshippers﴾, meaning, worship that is for you a characteristic of substance, whether in the present or the future.

Since the worship of God (glorified and exalted be He) was not well known among them before the Prophethood (al-Ba'tha), He expressed it with a form to which denial cannot be directed by them, namely the imperfect verb (al-mudari', the present/future tense), whose apparent meaning is the present or future (al-hal aw al-istiqbal), but which is intended to include the past, as Abu Hayyan and others mentioned in the surah of al-Hajj at ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and hinder from the way of God﴾ [al-Hajj: 25], that the imperfect is used to mean merely the occurrence of the act without regard to a specific time. So He said: ﴿I do not worship﴾, meaning, you have found from me the worship of Him, and it has been characterized by it now, in past time, and in future time, with a characterization that is substantial.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 109, verse 6:

When all of that had been stated, and the negation in the preceding sentences had begun with the one attributed to him (ﷺ), as an announcement of concern for his disavowal of them, it produced a sentence placed first, dealing with what pertains to them, in a manner that restricts it to them, as an emphasis on what had been expressed earlier of his disavowal of them: ﴿For you﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿is your religion﴾, that is, the one of which you know there is no foundation to rest upon and no proof to which it can be traced in any way. I do not share it with you in any way, and you do not turn away from it in any way. Rather, you will die upon it, some of you by natural death and others by being slain by my hand with the sword. ﴿And for me﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿is my religion﴾, from the broad garden of Islam up to [the highest -] station: [the station of] certainty (iqan) and excellence (ihsan). And you know, if you stripped your minds of desire and purified your thoughts of zealotry and obstinacy, that it is all evidence, criterion, light, proof and demonstration. You do not share it with me in any way, and you are not able to turn me away from it at all. This was thus one of the signs of prophethood (a'lam al-nubuwwah), in that many of them died afterward in disbelief, and God completed this religion for him. So God, glorified is He, was truthful in what He said, and the content of al-Kawthar was established with the most complete demonstration. As for those who believed after that, they are not intended, because they had not been deeply rooted in the attribute of disbelief nor firmly established in error and transgression, so the attribute of Islam and faith made them happy. He delivered all the sentences without emphasis, as an indication that they are so clear that there is no concealment in them at all. There is no doubt that their last, which is the exclusivity of each one to his religion, is their first, which conveys that he does not worship what they worship, nor do they worship what he worships. Thus the last became the first, and the joint is the connector. This is what the context indicates. There is in it no permission for disbelief, nor a prohibition of jihad requiring abrogation (naskh). Among the greatest proofs of its inimitability (i'jaz) is that it gathers meanings in its allusion and its brevity: its outcome is the cutting off of the hope of the people of disbelief that the Prophet (ﷺ) would approach them in associating anyone with their Lord at any time. This is among the greatest aims of the debate concerning it, in refuting the other [surah] in al-An'am, because that [verse] is the sixth in counting from the first, just as this [surah's verse] is the sixth in counting from the last: ﴿Shall I take other than God as a protector?﴾ [al-An'am: 14], ﴿Shall I seek other than God as a judge?﴾ [al-An'am: 114], ﴿Shall I seek other than God as a lord, when He is the Lord of everything?﴾ [al-An'am: 164], and other verses, and the connections and ends. This is what pertains to the meanings of its structures and arrangements as they are, and their orders and contexts and styles. Its written words are twenty-seven, from the basmalah's four words... [the] basmalah: thirty-one [words], to the four hidden pronouns, thirty-five, to the nine visible ones. These are forty-four words, of which thirteen are pronouns. These are the duration of the residence in Mecca, the honoured, before the Hijra, because they are in concealment like pronouns in the treasuries of secrets. Especially the first four of them, which correspond to the hidden pronouns. The non-pronouns are thirty-one, and their counterpart in years is the year thirty-one, which is the year in which Yazdajird, king of the Persians, the most disbelieving of the disbelievers and the most rebellious of the people of that time, was killed. The agreement of its words in number with the letters of al-Kawthar indicates that the few of his followers (ﷺ) are more and greater than the many of his hateful enemies, opponents and envious ones. This was shown by the testimony of the faces on the day of the conquest. The Muslims were ten thousand, and the disbelievers from Quraysh and those around them were countless in number. Their conduct on that day was what the excuse of Hamas attested to, who used to promise his wife that some of the Muslims would serve her. In his saying, when he had fled and was unable to close the door behind him, but said to her [instead]: "Close my door!" She said to him: "Where is what you used to promise me?" He said:

Indeed, if you had witnessed the day of al-Khandamah,
When Safwan fled and Ikrimah fled,

And they confronted them with the swords of the Muslims,
Cutting off every forearm and skull,

Striking, so that one hears nothing but the clamour,
Among them, a cry and a murmur,

You did not utter a single word of blame.

And this was despite the fact that the Prophet (ﷺ) had instructed them not to fight except those who began the fighting against them. And this is in addition to what happened with the people of Islam when they went against the disbelievers on the day of the Trench, while the polytheists were ten thousand, and they (the Muslims) did not reach a quarter of them, having no reinforcement from those around them and no helper except God. Rather, the enemies came upon them, as God, exalted, said: ﴿From above you and from below you﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10], ﴿And it only increased them in faith and submission﴾ [al-Ahzab: 22]. To this also pointed the reaching of the number of the words of victory, in their written forms and their technical forms, apparent and hidden, to the number of the written words of "al-Kafirun". This indicates that the weakest of the people of Islam is not weakened in resisting the people of disbelief, and is firmer than them in every attribute he desires. And God is the Granter of success.
